content: The roof that weathers the heaviest snow does not shake with the wind.
author: Japanese Proverbs
explanation: In the alpine villages of northern Japan, thatched roofs are built at steep sixty-degree angles to endure metric tons of frozen snow. Having withstood the crushing weight of winter, a mere gust of autumn wind cannot displace a single reed. Inner trials grant outer invulnerability.
practicalInsight: When petty critics or minor gossip swirl around you today, stand firm. You have survived far greater storms than this breeze.
reflectionPrompt: What severe trials have you survived in the past that should give you absolute courage against today's minor worries?
